title: A dense remnant
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Some core-collapse supernovae leave neutron stars, extremely dense compact remnants. Other outcomes, including black holes, depend on the mass and physics of the collapse.

misconception: A learner may choose: A new Solar System immediately
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: What can remain after some massive stars explode?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: What can remain after some massive stars explode? A neutron star. Some core-collapse supernovae leave neutron stars, extremely dense compact remnants. Other outcomes, including black holes, depend on the mass and physics of the collapse.
Visual caption: A compact neutron remnant. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
